issues.description: resolve(from, '..', s) silently assumes `from` is a file path, not a directory or URL
issues.detail: The change from resolve(s, from) to resolve(from, '..', s) is presented without a stated precondition on `from`. If `from` is already a directory, or a URL, or lacks a final path segment, '..' will climb one level too high. There is no invariant documented and no test pins the contract. State the precondition on `from` or normalize it.

issues.description: Synchronous readFileSync inside an async error-handling path is an unreasoned control-flow choice
issues.detail: getSourceMap performs blocking I/O (existsSync + readFileSync) on every stack frame during error serialization, inside Promise.all. No bound, no cache, no async alternative considered. The precondition (`file` is a real on-disk path the test runner is allowed to read) is unstated. Acceptable perhaps, but undefended.

issues.description: Fallback returning '{}' as a source map silently masks malformed references
issues.detail: createConvertSourceMapReadMap returns the string '{}' when the referenced map file does not exist. This is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE: a malformed sourceMappingURL is indistinguishable from a missing one, and downstream consumers receive a syntactically valid but semantically empty map. Either propagate the failure or log it; do not erase it.

issues.description: Correctness claim rests on a snapshot diff rather than reasoning
issues.detail: The only evidence of correctness is two updated snapshots showing .js -> .ts with shifted line numbers. TESTED-NOT-PROVED. There is no test that pins the resolve() semantics for edge inputs (absolute s, URL from, sources[] containing '..'), nor that the source-map extraction handles a file whose URL points outside the package. Snapshots show presence of behavior, not its correctness.

issues.description: Heuristic `!mod?.transformResult` as the external-module discriminator is undocumented and fragile
issues.detail: The comment asserts that external modules have a module-graph node but an empty transformResult. This is folklore, not specification. If Vite ever populates transformResult for an externalized module, source maps will be skipped silently. State the invariant Vite guarantees or query externality directly.

review.summary: The patch fixes a real bug but is delivered without the discipline its complexity demands. The one-line change in DecodedMap reverses argument order on resolve() with no stated precondition on `from`, and the new getSourceMap callback adds synchronous I/O and a heuristic externality check defended only by an inline comment. The '{}' fallback is defensive programming substituting for correctness. Snapshot diffs are presented as proof; they are evidence of behavior, not of reasoned correctness. The direction is right; the rigor is absent.
